headline: Democrats sweep Congress, oil −9%: $396M of BTC liquidations, mostly shorts, lift price above the true market mean; spot still at a discount.
summary: A short squeeze pushed price back above the true market mean of 77,627, and the short-term holders who bought at 76K are now in profit; STH-SOPR is back at 1.0021. Spot did not do the lifting: the Coinbase premium 7-day average is still −0.187%, ETFs lost a provisional $115.6M on Nov 3, and stablecoins are −2.15% over 7 days. Watch whether closes hold above 77,000 and whether US spot demand returns.

overview.lead: Once the election result landed, a short squeeze lifted price back above the true market mean and the new 76K layer flipped from loss to profit; but US spot, ETFs and stablecoins are all still pulling back, so this was leverage changing sides, not demand returning.
points: Today's finding: the 80,441 close is back above the true market mean of 77,627 (Bitview, Nov 4); STH-SOPR went 0.9954 → 1.0021 and the share of STH supply in profit rose from 30.25% on Nov 2 to 62.89%.

Derivatives did the pushing: CoinGlass shows $396M of BTC liquidations in 24 hours, 75.9% of them shorts (crypto.news, Nov 4); the Coinbase premium was −0.094% on the day and −0.187% on a 7-day average.
ETFs: provisional −$115.6M on Nov 3 (third outflow day); stablecoins $295.1B, −2.15% over 7 days; the exchange-supply supporting light turned off, now 3/6.
Bull day 27; no exit-framework trigger, and the gap to the 200-day MA widened to 9.0%.

news.title: Democrats win both the House and Senate and Trump says he accepts the result; the Dow +1,569 points (+3.03%), S&P 500 +1.58%, Nasdaq +1.44%, the Dow's best day since April 2025
news.read: The risk of a contested result is gone and risk assets rallied together; BTC rose 4.02% the same day, with a 0.63 30-day correlation to the Nasdaq. A change in Congress is a headwind for crypto legislation timing (see the CLARITY item), but the market traded the macro first. Better macro mood helps flows, but ETFs and the Coinbase premium have not followed yet; it does not change the cycle call.

news.read: Cheaper oil eases inflation and rate-hike pressure and the dollar weakened, a tailwind for BTC; our 10-year yield of 4.95% and real yield of 2.65% (FRED, Nov 3) do not yet reflect the day. findings.title: New 76K holders now in profit; loss selling is over, 84K is the supply overhead
findings.lean_why: Top-buyer supply has changed hands to new holders at 76K who now sit above cost, so loss selling from below has paused for now; the breakeven and LTH supply at 84K has not been absorbed.
findings.what: Question: with price back above the mean, will last week's 76K buyers hold, or sell to break even? The 80,441 close is back above the true market mean of 77,627, STH-SOPR went 0.9954 → 1.0021, and the share of STH supply in profit rose from 30.25% to 62.89% (Bitview, CheckOnChain, Nov 4).
findings.why: Participants: CheckOnChain (actual coin age, Nov 4) shows 3.713M STH BTC with an average cost of 75,292, thickest at 76K (651K) and 80K (570K); 30 days earlier (Bitview actual, Oct 4) it was 3.509M at 73,784, so STH supply grew by about 200K BTC in a month and its cost rose by 1,500. Estimated (Oct 4 → Nov 3), new supply concentrated at 76K (564K) and 80K (441K), and the most-moved STH supply sat at 84K (272K). Cost map: the close is about 6% above the 76K layer, so that layer flipped to profit; overhead, LTH supply is thickest at 84K (801K BTC) and URPD 84–86K is the thickest bucket above the close (1.082M BTC, Nov 3). Behavior check: SOPR is back at 1, but STH realized profit 3,863 vs loss 3,334 BTC (ratio 1.16, 2.47 a week ago), so profit-taking has not picked up; network-wide realized profit ÷ loss 7-day average 0.807 is still below 1. Contradiction: LTH 30-day net position −166,633 BTC (bitcoin-data, Nov 3) keeps widening, so supply overhead remains.
findings.alt: SOPR above 1 is a single day, driven by a price jump; STH-SOPR is daily and about 1 day late, so intraday loss selling can be averaged away. The estimated parts (30-day additions and spending) differ from actual STH totals by 3.2%, with 8.3% misplaced across buckets; per-UTXO data may count some post-Binance wallet moves as new 76K supply. LTH net change also includes coins automatically aging past 155 days, and it is not entity-adjusted.
findings.history: After each of this cycle's three prior STH-SOPR loss lows (Aug 1 0.9936, Aug 14 0.9946, Oct 30 0.9918) SOPR returned above 1; our STH/LTH supply split only exists since 2026-10-27, so there are no comparable samples, and there are no history stats for crossing the true market mean; background only.
findings.so: Logic chain: top-buyer short-term supply already sold at a loss into 76K (2026-11-03-1 confirmed), and the new holders now sit above cost, so loss selling from below has paused; the LTH supply and breakeven selling at 84K is still there, so a move higher meets supply first. Scenario (conditional, CheckOnChain Nov 4): at a close of 80,000 about 1.367M STH BTC are underwater; at 76,000 it jumps to 2.525M, so if the 76K layer fails again the underwater group nearly doubles at once. Market stage and exit framework did not move.
findings.next: By Nov 11: STH realized profit ÷ loss above 1.5 means the new holders start taking profit and the supply overhead gets tested, confirming; a close back below 77,000 (under the mean again) refutes.

findings.title: The post-election rally was short covering; US spot is still selling
findings.lean_why: A squeeze is one-off fuel that runs out once shorts are closed; the spot discount and ETF outflows did not improve, so the rally lacks a buyer that can carry it.
findings.what: On a 4.02% up day, the positions liquidated were mostly shorts, and US spot did not step in: CoinGlass shows $396M of BTC liquidations in 24 hours, 75.9% shorts, while the Coinbase premium 7-day average stayed at −0.187% (crypto.news and our data, Nov 4).
findings.why: Who pushed: on the derivatives side, weighted funding went 10.7% → 8.68%; price jumped while longs paid less, which points to shorts buying back rather than new longs chasing. Top 300 Hyperliquid accounts are short 7,891 BTC vs long 3,646 BTC (Nov 5 00:06 UTC), so shorts have not fully left. On the spot side, the Coinbase premium was −0.094% on the day (still negative) and the 7-day average is at percentile 0.7 of the series since 2026-01 (n=299); ETFs lost a provisional $115.6M on Nov 3, about −$1.16B over three days; stablecoins −2.15% over 7 days and −$12.2B over 30 (DefiLlama, Nov 4). Only Asia improved: the OKX OTC USDT discount narrowed from 1.137% to 0.838%. Cross-check: Glassnode (Nov 4, before the rally) also wrote that new demand from outside crypto is still missing.
findings.alt: Macro rallied at the same time (Dow +3.03%, oil −9%), so some buying may have come via CME or offshore spot that the Coinbase-vs-Binance premium cannot see; Nov 3 ETF data is provisional and Nov 4 is not out, so ETF flows on the post-election day are unknown. CoinGlass liquidations and our estimated liquidation bands use different methods and are not compared. Large Hyperliquid accounts may be market makers or hedgers.
findings.history: The previous 2 times the Coinbase premium 7-day average hit a 1-year low (2026-06-02, 06-28), price moved −7.8% and +7.3% over the next 30 days; after the previous 4 sharp 7-day stablecoin drops, the 30-day median was −8.0% (baseline −0.0%), n=4; too few samples, background only.
findings.so: What changed is position: price is back above the mean and a batch of shorts was cleared. What did not change is who is buying: US spot, ETFs and stablecoins are all still pulling back, so the rally's staying power needs spot confirmation. Conditional: a move to 82,000–83,000 would trigger another batch of estimated short liquidations (estimated, OKX only); forced short closes are market buys and could speed a rise, but that is still leverage fuel. Market stage and exit framework did not move.
findings.next: By Nov 11: a Coinbase premium 7-day average back above −0.05% means US spot has returned, refuting; a close back below 78,000 means the squeeze gains were given back, confirming.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Idling at Support
items.points: BTC about −10% from the September high, retesting the August breakout; STH supply in profit fell from ≥97.5% to about 38%; true market mean 77.7K, STH cost basis 75.7K, 200-day MA inside the 73–76K band, long liquidation risk at 73–76K and 60–63K, shorts clustered near 87K; Nov 27 and Dec 25 expiries hold $5.7B and $12.5B of OI with max pain at 80K and 76K; ETFs nearly −$1B over two weeks; after the past three midterms BTC fell another 15–50% within 2–10 weeks. Conclusion: holding 73–76K is a healthy reset within the August uptrend; a break below 73K points to a longer consolidation.
items.meaning: Data predates the Nov 4 rally; its support band matches our STH cost basis of 75,961 and 200-day MA of 73,181. Our Dec 25 max pain is 75,000 (Deribit), a different basis from its 76K. The midterm history is only 3 cases, so we do not use it for the call.
